Do you want to join the technological revolution? Tendium is looking for an ambitious individual in a customer-facing role, ready for the next step in their career! 
About Tendium
Tendium is the global pioneer in AI-driven public tender management, transforming how companies discover, analyse, and win government contracts. Our platform turns complex processes into something simple and transparent, empowering businesses to compete fairly for billions in public sector opportunities. We’ve been building our AI-native platform since 2018, leveraging a vast data moat, agentic AI, and tens of thousands of hours of R&D. Today, we serve large numbers of customers across Europe and are rapidly scaling.
If you want to know more about our culture and what you can expect when working at Tendium you can read more about it here.
The Job
As a Customer Success Manager, you will play a crucial role in ensuring our customers achieve success using our platform. You'll work closely with existing customers in the SME segment to secure renewals and identify opportunities for upselling and cross-selling. This position offers a blend of relationship building and technical support, making sure our customers get the most out of our product.
You’ll be part of our sales team, collaborating with marketing, sales, and product teams. We are looking for someone who is comfortable with both hands-on customer support and proactively identifying growth opportunities.
As a Customer Success Manager at Tendium, your main focus will be to:

Onboard, build and maintain strong relationships with customers to understand their goals, challenges, and pain points.

Develop and execute a customer success plan to help customers achieve their desired outcomes and business goals.

Provide ongoing support and guidance to customers using our platform.

Monitor and analyse customer usage and provide recommendations to improve the adoption and usage of our platform.

Engage with customers to ensure that they renew their subscriptions for our platform.

Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities and work with the sales team to close deals.

Be the voice of the customer and provide feedback to our product and engineering teams to improve our platform.

Collaborate with the marketing team to create customer case studies, testimonials, and other materials that showcase the success of our customers.

Resolve customer issues and ensure customer satisfaction.

Measure and report on customer success metrics, such as retention rate, customer satisfaction score (CSAT), and net promoter score (NPS).

Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for someone with experience in a customer success or customer-facing role within the tech or SaaS sector. To excel in this role, we believe you are entrepreneurial, proactive, and skilled at taking initiative and managing your own projects. As a key point of contact for our customers, strong communication and relationship-building abilities are essential.
Since you will be working at a leading SaaS company, it's crucial that you can quickly adapt to and stay ahead of the ongoing technical evolution of our product.
You Have:

Experience in a customer facing role within the SaaS/tech sector.

Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.

Ability to work independently and manage multiple customer accounts simultaneously.

Familiarity with AI technologies and an ability to adapt to new technologies.

Strong organisational skills with a keen attention to detail.

Proficient in Swedish and in English

Experience can come from either a business, sales, customer-facing, operational, or procurement-related background.

Bonus (but not mandatory) if you have:

Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, or a related field.

Experience with Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tools such as HubSpot or Salesforce.

Experience in a fast-paced start-up environment.

Experience and/or knowledge of public procurement processes.

Fluency in Norwegian or any additional European language is a plus.

Application
We look forward to your application. We recruit on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as possible. Successful candidates will initially be invited to an initial interview where you will have the opportunity to meet the team. 
Please find additional information on our recruitment process here.
To make this process even more efficient, feel free to sign in to your Connect profile and add your references at any stage.
If you’re ready to make an impact and grow with us, we want to hear from you.
_______________________
Equality and inclusion statement 
At Tendium, we value and celebrate diversity. We’re building a workplace where everyone feels that they belong, where your voice is heard, and your experiences are respected. Different perspectives fuel our creativity and drive innovation, and we’re always looking for people who can bring something new to the team. Whoever you are, wherever you're from, we’d love to hear from you.
Let’s shape the future together.

jobs.occupation: Systems Architect to Mycronic PCB Assembly Solutions
jobs.description:
Mycronic is a global high-tech company whose innovative solutions have been advancing electronics technology for over 50 years. Today we continue to grow and serve customers in an expanding variety of industries. What we do impacts the future of technology, and in turn, the way we live our lives tomorrow. We’re looking for people to join our talented, motivated and friendly team on the cutting-edge. Here, in an open, collaborative and flexible environment, you’ll work alongside leading industry experts and take on challenging projects that bring tomorrow’s electronics to life. Do you enjoy solving complex technical challenges and shaping the architecture of advanced products? Then you might be the person we’re looking for!
About the role
Mycronic has experienced strong growth in recent years, both organically and through acquisitions. With headquarters in Sweden, Mycronic is a global organization with subsidiaries, agents, and distributors in over 50 countries. In this role, you will be part of Mycronic's PCB Assembly Solutions division (PA), a leading provider of equipment and solutions for surface mount technology (SMT). Our solutions enable electronics manufacturers to adapt production quickly while maintaining high efficiency, ranging from individual systems for specific process steps to complete production lines and advanced software for assembly process management and connected factories. 
We Offer
A strategic role where you will have a significant influence on the direction of our world-leading Jet Printing product. 
The opportunity to work with new technology and contribute to innovation together with our Jet Printing core development team of 15 specialists across software, mechanics, electronics, configuration management, testing, product management, as well as collaborate with a wide range of functions across the company. 
A culture of innovation and collaboration, working together at our Kista office.

 
Work tasks
As a Systems Architect, you will lead the definition, development, and evolution of robust, scalable, and sustainable system architectures. You will provide the architectural perspective that connects our engineering disciplines and helps translate business and customer needs into technical direction. To do this effectively, you will invest the necessary time to truly understand our products and customers. This includes gaining firsthand experience of their perspective by using our systems during experiments, exploring new opportunities, and developing a deep understanding of how our solutions are used in practice.
Your responsibilities will include:
Lead and align cross-functional technical development, ensuring that software, electronics, mechanics, and mechatronics work together as an integrated system. 
Explore and drive the use of AI to deepen our understanding of the product, identify new opportunities, and improve how we develop and evolve our solutions.
Lead workshops and facilitate discussions around business and technical needs. Balance the overall architectural perspective with the necessary technical details while engaging others in developing concepts that meet customer and product requirements.
Support sales at customer-specific development by performing requirement analyses and product definition.
Establish, develop and share knowledge of current and future manufacturing technologies.

We are looking for
You are a true team player with an open and positive mindset, a strong sense of responsibility, and the ability to thrive in a global, fast-changing environment. You bring a pragmatic approach to product development, knowing when to push for improvements and when to recognize what already works well. You communicate clearly and effectively with people across different roles and areas of expertise, and take a thoughtful, structured approach to moving work forward, understanding what needs to be done, which competencies are needed, and when to involve the right people.
Furthermore, you have: 
A Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering Physics, Electronics, Mechatronics or similar. 
Solid experience in systems architecture for complex products combining hardware and software.
Solid knowledge of systems engineering, both theoretical and practical. 
Experience translating stakeholder requirements into technical solutions.
Strong ability to lead technical discussions and drive decisions.
Experience leading technical projects or product development activities.
Strong communication skills in English.

It will be considered a merit if you have:
Knowledge of Swedish. 
Proven experience in exploring and driving the use of AI in product development.

Other information
Start: By agreement 
Location: Stockholm, Kista 
Employment: Permanent, Full-time. 
Contact information: Senior Recruitment Consultant Johanna Sörell, johanna.sorell@academicwork.se. Recruitment Coordinator Vera Mohlin, vera.mohlin@academicwork.se. 
This recruitment process is managed by Academic Work. Mycronic requests that all questions regarding the position are directed to Academic Work.
Our selection process is continuous and the advert may close before the recruitment process is completed if we have moved forward to the next phase.

Our recruitment process
Problem solving- and personality test
Phone interview with Academic Work 
In-depth interview with Academic Work 
Interviews with Mycronic 
Reference checking & decision

SAVR is a fast-growing Swedish fintech company on a mission to reinvent investing. We empower investors with a platform that offers lower fees, greater transparency, and a radically improved experience.
We’re not just building another investment service — we’re reimagining how financial products should work for people, not just institutions. As part of our ambitious, innovative and curious team, you’ll help shape the future of investing in Sweden and beyond.
A quick note: This is not a traditional hiring process. While we're not actively looking to fill an immediate vacancy, we're always interested in meeting exceptional people who can help shape SAVR's future. If there's a strong mutual fit, we're open to exploring opportunities together
The Role – AI Engineer
As an AI Engineer with backend skills in our cross-functional team, you’ll join our tech team in Stockholm or Halmstad to build AI-powered product experiences end-to-end. You’ll work closely with fellow Software Engineers, Product Designers, and Product Managers to ship LLM-driven features such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, intelligent assistants, and automation, built for reliability, security, and great UX.
Our Tech Team Lead will manage and support your work, while reporting directly to our VP of Engineering. A glimpse into our tech stack: Python, SQL, Terraform, hosted on AWS, plus an AI stack that includes LLM APIs/open-source models, vector databases/similarity search, retrieval pipelines, evaluation tooling, and observability for production AI.
Your Mission
Build and ship LLM-powered product features (RAG, assistants, semantic search).

Productionize AI systems with guardrails, monitoring, evals, and cost/latency control.

Partner with product/design/engineering to turn use cases into measurable outcomes.

Build and maintain key platform features, APIs, and services, prioritizing scalability, reliability, and top-tier performance.

Provide direction and strategic insight on data related topics.

Additionally you will
Drive ideas and develop concepts from a tech perspective.

Explore ideas iteratively and refine them into production-quality solutions.

Contribute to improving the architecture, tech stack, and operational methods.

Improve our AI development workflow to support safe and reliable production AI.

Follow and promote good engineering practices to deliver high-quality products.

Engage in code reviews and foster a culture of continuous learning through constructive feedback.

Be a positive force for our team culture.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You...
4+ years of professional team-based software development experience, with at least some experience building ML/AI-powered features or systems in production.

Experience working with scalable, product-based environments, where you’ve shipped user-facing features and care about latency, reliability, and real-world constraints.

Solid understanding of backend systems and data modeling, enough to build reliable text retrieval, integrate with existing services, and reason about data quality, privacy, and access control in AI workflows.

Passion for applied AI, including prompt engineering, RAG, embeddings/vector search, LLM evaluation, fine-tuning, and model serving.

Strong collaboration skills and an open-minded approach to exchanging ideas.

Fluent in English and a team player who values diverse perspectives.

Swedish citizen or valid EU work permits (we cannot offer visa sponsorship for this role).

We’re seeking a motivated engineer with a broad skill set and a passion for applied AI, especially LLM-powered products, retrieval, and production-grade AI systems. You are someone who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and is eager to contribute to building something great.
Our Cultural DNA
At SAVR, we’re:

🧠 Open-minded – we embrace new ideas, diverse perspectives, and continuous learning
🚀 Bold – we take smart risks, move fast, and aren’t afraid to fail forward
🤝 Honest – we value transparency, feedback, and doing the right thing 
We’re a startup, so things can be a little messy — and that’s part of the thrill. If you thrive in building as a team and handling uncertainty, you will fit right in. 
What’s In It for You
You’ll join a product- and design-driven company where your work has real impact. We keep things lean, move fast, and genuinely care about the experience we deliver — for customers and for each other.
Here’s what we offer:
💻 Top-tier work gear
💰 Competitive salary
🏃‍♀️ Generous wellness allowance
🤒 Insurance package
🌱 Occupational pension and long-term savings support
🏢 Office-first approach to foster collaboration and quick decision-making — with flexibility when you need it (4+1)
🥗 Stocked pantry, plus regular social gatherings and wellness activities to keep energy and culture high

Our Commitment to Diversity
SAVR is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome people from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We believe diverse teams build better products and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.
Ready to Join Us?
We’d love to hear from you. Apply now or reach out with any questions — and let’s build something meaningful together.

Are you a results-oriented commercial leader who thrives at the heart of the business?
As Managing Director of Damstahl, you will lead a market-leading sales organisation and hold overall responsibility for sales, market development and financial performance. The head office is located in Malmö, with sales offices in Gothenburg and Stockholm. Sweden is the largest market and has an established sales organisation led by a Sales Director. The Swedish business generates revenue of approximately SEK 800-900 million and has 30 employees, 16 of whom are focused on sales. Damstahl also has a sales office and warehouses in Sweden, Norway and one salesperson in Finland.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Identifying new market segments and business opportunities
• Strengthening Damstahl’s market position and developing the product mix in prioritised areas
• Representing Damstahl in business negotiations, industry forums and trade fairs
• Overall responsibility for the company’s operations and performance in 3 Nordic countries
• Ensure that the strategy is translated into specific objectives and action plans.
• Be the culture ambassador and ensure that the organization's structure and capabilities support current and future business needs
You will lead the Swedish, Norwegian and Finnish operations with a clear mandate strategically. You will refer to the Damstahl’s Group CEO. The role involves approximately two days of travel per week, enabling you to remain close to the organisation, the business and market developments.
What we offer
This role is ideal for a leader who wants to develop an organization with a strong sales focus and who is motivated by doing business and creating growth, while benefiting from the long-term perspective and stability of a successful and well-established company.
Damstahl’s ambition is to become one of Europe’s three leading distributors within its field. Its strategy is based on increasing market share, developing the product mix and identifying new areas of growth. Digitalization is an important part of Damstahl’s strategy and customer offering. Damstahl has a fully developed webshop, EDI and ERP integrations, and also offers AI-based services.
Who are you?
You are a results-oriented commercial leader who wants to stay close to the business. You understand how warehousing and logistics contribute to commercial success and can demonstrate, through documented results, that you have created profitable growth as a Sales Director or Managing Director within B2B—preferably in an industrial business with warehousing operations.
You have a strong ability to turn plans into action and can analyze market developments and the competitive landscape, translating these insights into clear commercial priorities. Experience from steel, metals, technical distribution or a related industrial sector is a significant advantage. Knowledge of tubes, fittings and flanges is particularly valuable, as this is a key area for growth. Fluency in spoken and written English and Swedish is required.
About Damstahl
Damstahl AB’s head office is located in Malmö, with sales offices in Gothenburg and Stockholm. The company also has a sales office in Norway and sales representation in Finland. Whilst the Damstahl Group has its headquarter in Skanderborg, Denmark.
Damstahl is part of the NEUMO Ehrenberg Group, a family-owned industrial group with approximately 2,250 employees and annual revenue of around EUR 800 million.
· Damstahl Group generates revenue of approximately EUR 350 million
· The Group has around 290 employees
· More than 70,000 tonnes of stainless steel are distributed annually
· Warehousing and distribution capacity is located in Denmark, Sweden and Norway
Damstahl’s competitive strength is built on extensive product expertise, high availability and a comprehensive Nordic and European warehousing and distribution network. We offer a broad and extensive range of stainless steel products, including sheets, bars, tubes, fittings and flanges. Through the Group, the offering also includes aluminium and other metals.
The Skanderborg facility includes an automated high-bay warehouse with capacity for approximately 10,000 tonnes of stainless steel The extensive warehousing structure ensures high product availability and short lead times across the Nordic markets. 
The Malmö facility includes a fully automated warehouse with the capacity of 4 400 m/2. The operation running from 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM with a total staff of five, plus three people handling logistics and returns, along with a Team Leader for that group. https://www.damstahl.com/sv/
Application
Damstahl is collaborating with Charlotte Olsson at Insikta AB on this recruitment. If you have any questions, please contact Charlotte Olsson on +46 70 602 19 11 or at charlotte@insikta.se.
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Naturally, all enquiries and applications will be treated confidentially. To apply, simply submit your CV together with a brief explanation of why you are interested in the role.

Why Doktor.se
Doktor.se is Sweden's largest digital healthcare provider. We combine physical clinics with a digital platform serving millions of consultations per year across Sweden, Germany, and Norway. Our 25-person engineering team has startup autonomy inside a profitable, international organization with 1,000+ employees and over 1B SEK in revenue.
We run OpenAI and Anthropic models in production across patient and clinician workflows, and that footprint is growing fast.
What you'll do
Our infrastructure works, but it was built to solve yesterday's problems. We need someone who can help us get to where we want to be — not maintain what we have, but reshape it. If you want a place where everything is already figured out, this isn't it. If you want to build something better, here's what you'd own:

Build a deployment platform where teams ship their own services without asking you for permission.

Design infrastructure that is secure by default, so teams don't have to think about encryption, network isolation, or data residency. It just works.

Create deployment pipelines where security scanning, policy checks, and compliance happen automatically, invisible when everything is fine, loud when something needs attention.

Support and scale infrastructure for AI workloads, we run models in production across our platform, and that footprint is growing.

Set up observability that gives teams real insight into their own services, useful dashboards, alerts that mean something, not noise that everyone ignores.

Work closely with developers to understand what slows them down, and then fix it. Not by doing it for them, but by making it easy for them to do it themselves.

Maintain and evolve our cloud account structure, networking, and identity management across multiple regions and products.

You will report to to, and work close with, our Head of Product and Technology. You will be the go to person in technical strategical questions and the technical sounding board — advising on complex technical decisions and translating product/business direction into what's actually feasible.

Some weeks you'll write infrastructure code. Some weeks you'll pair with a developer to debug a slow service. Some weeks you'll design how a new product gets its own isolated infrastructure. The common thread: you make the teams around you better.
Make developers faster, not more dependent on you.
What we're looking for
You've built and operated Kubernetes in production. Not just deployed a Helm chart once, you've debugged networking issues, designed RBAC policies, and thought about how multiple teams share a cluster without stepping on each other.

You know AWS well. Accounts, networking, IAM, KMS. You have opinions about what should live in Kubernetes and what genuinely needs to be an AWS managed service, and you lean toward keeping things in Kubernetes where possible.

You've worked with GitOps and infrastructure as code. Flux, ArgoCD, Terrafor, specific tools matter less than the principle: infrastructure changes go through pull requests, are reviewed, and are auditable.

You understand developers because you are one. You can read their code, understand their pipelines, and have meaningful conversations about architecture.

You think about security as something you design into systems, not something you review at the end.

You have opinions, and you can change them when someone makes a better argument.

University degree in computer science, engineering, or equivalent experience.

Tech stack
Cloud - AWS (multi-account, multi-region)
Orchestration - Kubernetes / EKS
IaC - Terraform
CI/CD - GitHub Actions
Languages - Python, TypeScript
AI - OpenAI, Anthropic (in production and tooling)
Observability - Datadog / Grafana (you'll shape this)
What we offer
Real influence. You'll shape how our platform works, not just operate what someone else designed.

Healthcare context. Patient data, regulatory compliance, and real consequences for getting it wrong. What you build actually matters.

Small team, direct impact. 25 engineers, your work is visible, not lost in a machine.

Autonomy. No micromanagement, no endless approval chains.

AI in production. We're running LLMs in patient and clinician workflows today, the infrastructure needs to grow with that.

Collective agreement, 30 days vacation, wellness allowance, personal development budget.

Practical details
Start: As soon as we find the right person. We'll accommodate your notice period.

Employment: Permanent, full-time. Six month probation period.

Location: On-site, Monday–Thursday at Sveavägen 63, Stockholm. Fridays are flexible.

Language: English is our working language in tech. Swedish is a bonus.

Work permit: You must already have the right to work in Sweden.

Contact: Karin Bergström, Head of Product and technology

We handle recruitment internally — no agencies, no consultants, no external recruiters.

Job Scope 
High level purpose of function. 

A Vision Automation Engineer in a cell manufacturing company plays a key role in developing, optimizing, reverse-engineering, and maintaining machine vision and optical inspection systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. They are responsible for programming, troubleshooting, and improving cameras, lighting configurations, and image processing algorithms, supporting both legacy production line re-commissioning and new vision system installations. The role also includes ensuring accurate data transfer, system connectivity, and smooth communication with PLCs, SCADA, and upper-level MES platforms to enable inline defect traceability, dimensional inspection, and digital integration. Close collaboration with production, engineering, and maintenance teams is required to identify and implement solutions that improve quality, throughput, and equipment uptime. A strong focus is placed on continuous improvement, safety, and scalability to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle battery production. 

Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to) 
Participate in HAZOP sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards relating to equipment control and programming.  
Responsible for the FATs of the equipment (Project timeline dependent).  
Lead vision system integration and optical calibration during equipment commissioning and line re-starts (Project timeline dependent). 
Develop and reverse-engineer the vision inspection systems to be implemented in the production and logistics equipment in the factory, as well as the relevant specifications and documentation. 
Author and review engineering design documentation (Specifications, Functional design, Logic diagrams, Test Cases, Test Records).  
Train and mentor new engineers, and educate other support functions on machine vision, optics, and quality inspection gates. 
Code review and test of suppliers' vision software and algorithmic work within the projects to validate specified defect detection thresholds (Gauge R&R) and to ensure the quality and reliability of the data transferred from the equipment to the upper-level systems. 
Participate in R&D activities for piloting of new technologies and their suitability to production environments. 
Define and improve the factory blueprint, general specifications and ways of working in collaboration with the extended automation and digitalization teams. (Project timeline dependent). 
Contribute to technical improvements, development and optimization of software processes internally in the automation team 
The role requires regular presence on the production floor, with a minimum of approximately 25% of working hours spent on-site. Depending on project needs (such as line re-commissioning), there may be periods where up to 100% of working hours are required on the shop floor. 
Develop and maintain machine vision and image processing programming standards. 
Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focussing on growth and development. 
Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business. 

Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 

Qualifications and Experience 
Bachelors Degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical, Automation, Robotics, Software Engineering or similar. 
Minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience within Industrial Automation in process-driven or discrete manufacturing industries such as: Battery Cell, Automotive, Chemical, Paper, Semiconductors, Pharma, Food, Warehouses, etc. 
Experience of working with industrial camera systems, optical components, and lighting techniques, including the selection, configuration, and calibration of camera hardware for manufacturing inspection and process control applications 
Experience in the design, configuration, and deployment of machine vision systems including cameras, lighting, and vision software platforms such as Cognex, Halcon, or equivalent, with experience integrating vision outputs into PLC, SCADA, and MES environments via OPC connectivity. 
Experience developing and optimising image processing pipelines and vision algorithms for applications such as defect detection, pattern recognition, and dimensional verification, with familiarity with industrial communication protocols for vision system integration. 
Experience in writing technical documentation including inspection requirement specifications, algorithm validation reports, vision system configuration records, functional design, UML, test cases, and test records. 
Experience with image processing software and programming tools relevant to industrial vision applications, such as Python, C++, OpenCV, or equivalent vision libraries, with the ability to develop, test, and optimise vision algorithms for real-time manufacturing environments 
Experienced continuous improvement and root cause analysis. 

Specific skills 
Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems. 
Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices for manufacturing systems. 
Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment. 
Ability to document technical problems concisely. 
Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams. 
Ability to work within varying environments including clean-rooms and dry-rooms, while wearing appropriate PPE. 
Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments. 
A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.

At SSC Space, you are part of something bigger. 
Every day, our people contribute to missions that expand knowledge, support critical services, and help society benefit from space. We believe the best results come from passionate experts who collaborate, take ownership, and turn ambitious ideas into reality.  
As Mission Manager, you will oversee customer payload missions from initial planning through launch and post-mission review. Working in an international environment, you will bring together customers, brokers, satellite manufacturers, launch vehicle providers and operators, and internal teams to define mission requirements and coordinate delivery against agreed objectives. 
You will serve as the customer's primary point of contact throughout the mission lifecycle, combining technical coordination, project management, and customer relationship management. jobs.occupation: Frontier Fellow - Forward Deployed AI Engineer
jobs.description:
The most valuable product development happens where the product meets reality. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you work at that intersection: you turn AI agents into production-ready customer solutions and bring what you learn back into the product.
We call this role a Frontier Fellow: part senior engineer, part trusted technical advisor and part bridge between our customers, delivery teams and the HiveAI product team. HiveAI is Fellowmind's agent platform.
About the role
You belong to the HiveAI product organisation, but you will do much of your work alongside our implementation teams and customers.
Building one agent is easy now. Building agents a business can rely on every day is not. That's where you come in: you take on the hardest problems in our customer projects and solve them.
The job doesn't end when the solution works. You turn what you learn into HiveAI: when relevant, functionality, patterns and components built for one customer become reusable capabilities that help the next customer and everyone else.
What you will do
Fix the hard parts. Step in where agents meet real business systems, identity and users, and make them work. When shared components fall short, build your own.
Get AI agents into use, fast. Work with our delivery teams from the first customer conversation to go-live. Put a working first version in front of users within days.
Be a front runner. Help customers and Fellowmind teams make sound architecture decisions, challenge approaches that won't scale and explain technical trade-offs clearly.
Shape HiveAI. Share recurring requirements and architectural insights with the HiveAI development team.
Raise the bar for everyone. Share knowledge, patterns and best practices so implementation teams can deliver HiveAI successfully on their own.

What you might build
An agent that takes over a whole task, like handling supplier invoices or preparing quotes, and asks a person when a decision is needed.
An agent that works across ERP, CRM and the intranet on behalf of the person who asked.
A team of agents that share one business process, handing work to each other.
The tools, MCP servers and integrations they need.

Who are you?
You are an experienced engineer who enjoys being close to both the technology and the customer.
You can't stop building agents, and you want people to actually use them. You'd rather show something that works than a design document. You make good decisions without all the information, and you're as comfortable in a customer workshop as in a code review.
You bring:
Coding agents such as GitHub Copilot as your everyday way of working, and the judgement to know which generated code will hold up in production.
At least 4 years of professional software development experience, with strong skills in at least one programming language and solid engineering habits: branches, pull requests and tests
Experience taking software into production, where security, reliability and performance matter.
Practical knowledge of AI models and agents: how they behave, what they cost, how to measure them with evals.
Working knowledge of Azure, Entra ID, On-Behalf-Of and least privilege.
Direct customer-facing experience, from technical discovery and workshops to architecture discussions and communication with senior stakeholders.
A good understanding of modern product development, including when customer-specific functionality should become a reusable product capability.

Nobody ticks every box. If you're strong in several of these and know where to find help for the rest, we'd like to hear from you.
What is HiveAI?
At Fellowmind, we're building HiveAI, a platform for developing, deploying and operating AI solutions at scale. It gives enterprises a secure and scalable foundation to move beyond isolated experiments, so AI becomes part of how the business operates.
At its core is the HiveAI Agent Platform, built on Microsoft Azure, which runs AI agents securely and at scale. Around it sits the HiveAI Agent Lifecycle, which helps organisations develop, manage and continuously improve their agents over time.
Why Fellowmind?
Fellowmind combines deep industry knowledge and personal guidance with Microsoft cloud technology across ERP, cloud infrastructure, data & AI, CRM, intranet and Modern Workplace. We are an international organisation with more than 2,000 colleagues across Europe.
Our culture is built around putting people at the heart of what we do. We value collaboration, personal responsibility, development and the freedom to find a sustainable balance between work and life.
The practicalities
Start: As soon as possible, and of course we'll take your notice period into account.
Scope: Full-time.
Location: This role can be based in Sweden, Denmark or the Netherlands, from one of our Fellowmind offices.
Travel: You will work with regional teams and customers across Fellowmind, so travel is a natural part of the role.
Language: Professional proficiency in English and the local language of your country of employment: Swedish, Danish or Dutch.
Process: We start with a screening interview, followed by in-depth interviews, assessments or case work, and reference checks.
